Subject: Mosaic security questionnaire: data locality & retention for Redwood hosted API

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for taking this on. Attached is the short questionnaire our security team pulled together focused narrowly on where data lives, what gets persisted, and how deletion requests are handled for hosted API customers. We’re trying to map whether we can keep PII-derived outputs in our US tenancy only — and we need specifics for procurement.

Top items we care about:
- Which regions hold inference request payloads, intermediate caches (KV/prefix), and long-term backups?
- How long do you retain request payloads, model-generated outputs, and logs by default? Can we set custom TTLs per tenant?
- When Mosaic requests full erasure for a tenant, describe the steps and timelines for propagation across caches, backups, and analytics replicas.
- Are backups encrypted with customer-managed keys (CMK) or Redwood-managed KMS?

We’ve filled out the spreadsheet and flagged the most critical questions. Can you respond inline or provide a short narrative we can include in our security review?

Appreciate a reply by Wednesday if possible.

Best,

Elena — thanks for the questionnaire. I’ve answered inline in the attached spreadsheet and summarized the key points below to make it easy for procurement & your security team. If you want, Irene (CC) can confirm kernel-level persistence behavior and our backup retention details.

Summary for Mosaic (hosted API):
1) Regions & where data may be present:
   - Request payloads and immediate inference state: processed in the region you select for the tenant (we support region pinning; Mosaic can request US-East-1 only).
   - Short-term KV/prefix caches: located on the serving nodes in the same region; TTLs are configurable per-tenant and default to 1 hour for session caches.
   - Longer-lived logs and analytics: aggregated in US logs clusters (US-East-1) by default; can be routed to your customer-owned S3 via our log-forwarding integration.
   - Snapshots/backups: nightly snapshots stored in the selected region's S3 buckets (default US-East-1 for US tenants). We do not replicate snapshots to other regions unless cross-region DR is explicitly enabled by the customer.

2) Default retention periods (hosted API):
   - Request payloads (raw input) for debugging: retained up to 30 days by default; customers may reduce to 0 days for ephemeral mode.
   - Model outputs (generated text) stored for 30 days by default for quality monitoring and safety review; adjustable per tenant via account settings.
   - Serving caches (KV/prefix): default TTL 1 hour; configurable down to 0 (no caching) or longer as needed for throughput optimization.
   - Audit and operational logs: retained 90 days by default; extended retention available as an add-on.

3) Deletion / erasure flow (tenant deletion request):
   - Step 1: Customer initiates erasure via Console API or support ticket — we start a coordinated purge job.
   - Step 2: Active caches and prefix KVs for the tenant are invalidated immediately; effective removal from serving path occurs within minutes.
   - Step 3: Operational indexes and analytic aggregates are updated asynchronously; propagation completes within 48 hours under standard load.
   - Step 4: Snapshots/backups: retention windows mean historical snapshots may contain tenant data until the next snapshot rotation/purge. We schedule specific backup purges; typical final purge completes within 7 days after the erasure job start.
   - SLA/Assurance: Full removal from all live systems and scheduled backups targeted within 7 days, with an interim confirmation when caches & primary stores are cleared (usually within 48 hours).

4) Encryption & key management:
   - Default: snapshots and backups encrypted with Redwood-managed KMS (SSE-KMS).
   - Enterprise option: customer-managed CMK available for Private and Dedicated customers. For Hosted API enterprise tiers we support an integration to use your CMK in your own AWS account when requested (requires onboarding).

5) Additional controls:
   - Data residency enforcement: tenant pinning to a regional control plane to prevent routing to other regions.
   - Audit logs: we provide an exportable evidence pack (S3 or shared Drive) for erasure jobs and access history.

Irene — I’ve highlighted two technical items in the sheet where a kernel-level confirmation is useful: (a) whether in-memory KV snapshots are ever flushed to disk during OOM/eviction, and (b) exact backup rotation/purge mechanics.

Next steps: I’ll attach the completed spreadsheet and a short one-page playbook describing the erasure timeline. Happy to hop on a quick call with your security team to walk through.

Thanks,

Elena — quick technical clarifications from the runtime side:

- In-memory KV/prefix cache durability: serving nodes keep KV data in RAM for low-latency access. We do not persist active KV cache state to disk under normal operation. If a node is drained or fails, rebuilding the cache happens from the upstream sequence (there is no deliberate disk snapshot of KV cache). In exceptional recovery scenarios, ephemeral snapshot artifacts (log-based) may temporarily exist but are ephemeral and discarded on restart.

- Backup snapshot purge mechanics: nightly snapshots are immutable objects in the tenant-scoped bucket with lifecycle rules. When a tenant erasure request is processed we trigger a targeted lifecycle deletion for objects tagged with the tenant ID; the deletion job is queued and processed within AWS S3 lifecycle/our orchestration — expected completion window 72 hours, though we target 7 days for full cross-system reconciliation (search indexes, analytics, and any replicated audit exports).

- Metrics and analytics exports: we can configure metrics ingestion to exclude raw payloads and only emit aggregate telemetry to your analytics workspace.

If Mosaic requires CMK control for backups in Hosted API, that is feasible via the enterprise onboarding path; we’ll need a short runbook and permission grant.

Happy to provide a short technical addendum for procurement.

—Irene
Irene Choi
